text:
maria-cs: Heads up — VeloPay reported surge of 429s and p95 latency spikes on their Dedicated cluster starting ~10:45 UTC. Support ticket #4592. Console shows burst credits = 0. They say autoscaler didn't add capacity fast enough. Can SRE triage?

olivia-support: copying logs + repro from the customer. They sent a curl that reproduces 429s quickly:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-llm-xl","input":"<payload>"}'
```

maria-cs: paste from their control-plane logs (redacted):
```
[10:44:51] admission_control: REJECT token_rate=430 tps_limit=250 burst_credits=0 headroom_tokens=120 request_id=abc123
[10:44:52] response: 429 Too Many Requests
[10:45:10] p95_latency_ms=960
```

raj-sre: Looking. Initial hypothesis: admission control exhausted burst credits, autoscaler cooldown + provisioning latency means we didn't hit target capacity in time. Also possible noisy neighbor on same GPU host. Can you pull per-node GPU util + admission metrics? Run admin metrics query like:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_ADMIN" "https://infra-api.internal/v1/metrics?cluster=dedicated-velopay&window=5m"
```

ling-enginfra: pulled metrics — one host (gpu-16-03) at NVLink/NVSwitch 95-99% util during spike. Another tenant (analytics-ark) showed large batched embedding job at 10:43-10:46 that consumed tokens. Autoscaler config has cooldown_seconds=300 and min_replicas=1 for this pool, so scale-up started late and nodes were still provisioning. I kicked a manual scale + allocated emergency burst credits from org reserve.

simon-oncall: manual actions applied at 10:52: +2 GPUs added to the pool, emergency 10k burst credits applied to VeloPay. Immediately after: 429s dropped from ~22% to ~1%, p95 latency dropped 960ms -> ~210ms. Filing follow-up postmortem. :thumbsup:

olivia-support: sent quick mitigation guidance to customer: throttle client concurrency (suggested parallel connections 50 -> 12), add retry/backoff, enable streaming to reduce token-in-flight. Also offered temporary reserved capacity and proposed autoscaler tweak (lower cooldown and increase headroom_tokens). Customer agreed to a short call.

maria-cs: shared the admission_control block we plan to propose for them (for reference):

```
admission_control:
  tps_limit: 250
  burst_credits: 5000
  headroom_tokens: 600
  cooldown_seconds: 90
```

elaine-accounts: I'll propose a reserved + pre-warmed option in the next contract amendment. Customer is open to increasing their commit to cover typical peak windows. Scheduling call tomorrow.

raj-sre: Action items I/O: [INF-3127] add per-tenant spike detector + alert when burst_credits < 20% or sustained tps > tps_limit; [OPS-867] evaluate lowering autoscaler cooldown for Dedicated pools with bursty workloads; [ENGINFRA-421] add tenant isolation flags so huge batched jobs can't share specific GPU hosts with low-latency tenants. Also document headroom planning guidance and add to support KB. I'll create the tickets.

maria-cs: Thanks team — logging ticket refs for the customer follow-up: INF-3127, OPS-867, ENGINFRA-421. Noting customer pleased with the fast mitigation; they want guidance on sizing headroom and recommended client configs.

deploy-bot: automated note: infra-node-add initiated by simon-oncall at 2026-03-16T10:52:10Z; nodes 2/2 active at 2026-03-16T10:57:34Z.

olivia-support: Summary for thread to add to ticket: cause=burst credits depleted + autoscaler provisioning lag; contributing=noisy neighbor embedding job; short-term fix=manual scale + emergency burst credits + client throttling; long-term=autoscaler cooldown tuning, per-tenant spike alerts, reserved capacity discussion. Sending to customer now.

maria-cs: closing loop here — will post meeting notes after contract call. Thanks everyone. :pray:
